name: Notion Guard
description:
Notion Guard is a governance-first Notion integration for small teams that want AI-assisted page and database work without silent or unrestricted changes.

Commands: notion.search (search pages/data sources shared with the integration); notion.get_data_source_schema (inspect a data source's property names, types, option values); notion.query_data_source (filter/sort/page a data source's rows); notion.get_page (read one page's properties); notion.get_page_content (read a page's or block's content); notion.list_users (list workspace users, for addressing people by name); notion.create_page (create a page, approval-gated); notion.update_page_properties (update properties or trash status, approval-gated); notion.append_blocks (append content blocks, approval-gated); notion.create_comment (add a comment or discussion reply, approval-gated).

Six reads execute immediately. Four approval-gated writes use RailCall's preview-approve-execute flow; Notion changes only after a human approves the exact payload.

Real Notion REST API, no mocks. Checks HTTP status on every response, treats network failures and 5xx responses during a write as an unknown outcome, never auto-retries a mutation, never presents a failed operation as successful.

Quick start: create an internal integration at https://www.notion.so/my-integrations, share pages/databases with it, save the secret as NOTION_API_KEY on the muhammad-akif-janjua-notion-guard::notion card in RailCall Studio Integrations (not the plain notion card), reload Modules, begin with notion.search then notion.get_data_source_schema before your first write.

Example calls: notion.search {"query":"quarterly roadmap","page_size":10}; notion.get_data_source_schema {"database_id":"<32-char id from the database URL>"}; notion.query_data_source {"data_source_id":"<id>","page_size":10}; notion.get_page {"page_id":"<id>"}; notion.get_page_content {"page_id":"<id>"}; notion.list_users {"page_size":20}; notion.create_page {"parent_type":"data_source_id","parent_id":"<id>","properties_json":"{\"Name\":{\"title\":[{\"text\":{\"content\":\"Ship the demo\"}}]}}"}; notion.update_page_properties {"page_id":"<id>","properties_json":"{\"Status\":{\"select\":{\"name\":\"Done\"}}}"}; notion.append_blocks {"block_id":"<id>","children_json":"[{\"object\":\"block\",\"type\":\"paragraph\",\"paragraph\":{\"rich_text\":[{\"text\":{\"content\":\"Checked.\"}}]}}]"}; notion.create_comment {"parent_type":"page_id","parent_id":"<id>","text":"Need a human on this."}.

Limitations: only sees pages/databases shared with it. Results are bounded for readable receipts.

Built for the RailCall Track A module contest.

contest:2026Q3

Zero model-provider destinations in the signed manifest. Notion REST traffic is the only business integration path, not an LLM call; the handler never invokes a model-provider SDK or RailCall model-completion primitive.

query.description: Free-text search across page and data-source titles; omit to list everything the integration can see.

object_type.description: Restrict results to 'page' or 'data_source'; omit to return both.

start_cursor.description: Cursor from a previous call's next_cursor, to fetch the next page.

page_size.description: Max results per page (up to 50, default 20).

data_source_id.description: The data source's ID directly; provide this or database_id.

database_id.description: A database's ID (e.g. copied from its Notion URL); resolved to its data source automatically when the database has exactly one.

data_source_id.description: The data source to query, from notion.search or notion.get_data_source_schema.

filter_json.description: Notion filter object as a JSON string, e.g. {"property":"Status","select":{"equals":"Done"}}; omit to return all rows.

sorts_json.description: Notion sorts array as a JSON string, e.g. [{"property":"Name","direction":"ascending"}]; omit for default order.

start_cursor.description: Cursor from a previous call's next_cursor, to fetch the next page.

page_size.description: Max rows per page (up to 50, default 20).

page_id.description: The Notion page's ID (from notion.search or a Notion URL) - the bare ID, not the full URL.
The page to read top-level content from; provide this or block_id.

block_id.description: A specific block's ID (e.g. a toggle) to read its children from, as returned by an earlier call to this same command.

start_cursor.description: Cursor from a previous call's next_cursor, to fetch the next page.

page_size.description: Max blocks per page (up to 50, default 20).

start_cursor.description: Cursor from a previous call's next_cursor, to fetch the next page.

page_size.description: Max users per page (up to 50, default 20).

parent_type.description: 'data_source_id' to create a row in a database, or 'page_id' to create a subpage.

parent_id.description: The ID of the parent named by parent_type.

properties_json.description: The new page's properties as a JSON object string, matching the parent data source's schema (see notion.get_data_source_schema); for a plain subpage, just the title property.

children_json.description: Initial content blocks as a JSON array string (up to 100); omit to create an empty page.

icon_emoji.description: A single emoji to use as the page's icon; omit for no icon.

properties_json.description: Properties to change as a JSON object string, matching the page's schema; only the properties included are changed.

in_trash.description: true moves the page to Notion's trash, false restores it; omit to leave trash status unchanged.

commands.title: Append Blocks to a Notion Page

block_id.description: The page or block ID to append content to.

children_json.description: Content blocks to append as a JSON array string (1-100), e.g. [{"object":"block","type":"paragraph","paragraph":{"rich_text":[{"text":{"content":"Done."}}]}}].

position.description: 'end' (default) or 'start' - where the new blocks land relative to existing content.

parent_type.description: 'page_id' or 'block_id' to start a new comment thread, or 'discussion_id' to reply to an existing one.

parent_id.description: The ID of the parent named by parent_type.
